title: Compress Quantities to Fit Storage
statement:
An array `a` of `n` integers must be stored in exactly `I` bytes (that is, `8 * I` bits) of memory. If the array contains `k` distinct values, every element is stored using `ceil(log2(k))` bits (so an array with a single distinct value needs `0` bits per element). The array fits when `n * ceil(log2(k)) ≤ 8 * I`.

To make the array fit you may choose two integers `x ≤ y` and **clamp** every element into the range `[x, y]`: an element smaller than `x` becomes `x`, an element larger than `y` becomes `y`, and elements already inside `[x, y]` stay as they are. The numbers `x` and `y` do not have to appear in the array.

An element is **changed** if its value is different after clamping. Choose `x` and `y` so that the clamped array fits in `I` bytes while the number of changed elements is as small as possible.

Print that minimum number of changed elements (it is `0` if the array already fits).
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `I`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[0] ... a[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum number of changed elements.

examples.explanation: 8 bits for 6 elements allows only 1 bit per element, so at most 2 distinct values may remain. Clamping to `[3, 4]` gives `3 3 3 4 4 4`, which needs 6 bits. Only the elements 3 and 4 survive, so 4 elements change.

Again 1 bit per element, so 2 distinct values at most. Clamping to `[5, 7]` turns the three 9s into 7s (3 changes); `[7, 9]` turns the three 5s into 7s (also 3). Keeping `[5, 9]` would leave 3 distinct values and need 2 bits, which does not fit.
8 bits for 10 elements gives 0 bits per element, so every element must become the same value. Clamping to `[4, 4]` keeps the four 4s and changes the other 6.

hints: The bits per element depend only on the number of distinct values. Work out the largest number of distinct values `K` allowed: `ceil(log2(k)) ≤ floor(8 * I / n)`.
Clamping to `[x, y]` keeps exactly the elements whose value lies in `[x, y]`, so you want the range holding the most elements while containing at most `K` distinct values.
Sort the distinct values with their counts and slide a window of at most `K` consecutive distinct values, tracking the largest total count. The answer is `n` minus that total.
